clue.text: Observe derisory response not engaging all hearts

indicators.note: not engaging means the word all is kept out, removed from the jeer

parts.note: a catcall is a jeering whistle or shout of derision
the letters of all, taken as written
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Someone notes a mocking reaction that fails to win everyone's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ALL from CATCALL to leave CATC, then add H for hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something is to notice or perceive it, as in catching sight of a thing.

clue.text: Social group dispersed by end of Empire

parts.note: cast means thrown or scattered about

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of Empire

explanation.surface: A class of people scattered as the Empire fell.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary class in a rigid social hierarchy.

clue.text: Time to take a different line, heading off predator

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to digress is to wander off the main line of a discussion

explanation.surface: Time to change course, sidestepping a hunting animal.
explanation.walkthrough: T, then DIGRESS without its first letter: IGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, a big-cat hunter.

clue.text: Warm feelings leading to embrace around right spot in front of the fire?

definitions.text: spot in front of the fire?

indicators.note: leading to means the feelings come first

parts.note: the heart is the seat of warm feelings, affection

indicators.note: around means the embrace goes round the right letter

parts.note: a hug is an embrace

explanation.surface: Affection leads to a cuddle by the fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is playful: a rug is a spot rather than a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is a small rug placed on the floor before a fireplace, a cosy place to sit.

clue.text: The CIA's wrong-footed about American meeting old European leader

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
wrong-footed suggests the letters are put out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters of The CIA's, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: meeting means the American letter sits right beside the old one

explanation.surface: American intelligence is caught out over a meeting with a former European statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split after their first letter to take in the American and old letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland, the head of a European government.

clue.text: Sentence: "Chinese invading West?" — something seen in SF story?

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

indicators.note: invading means the Chinese piece goes inside the West piece

parts.note: Mae West, the film star
Chin is a Chinese dynasty, also spelt Qin

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a Chinese invasion of the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' with a question mark is the actress Mae West, not the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: H.G. Wells's science fiction story The Time Machine features a device for travelling through time.

clue.text: Admit feeling unhappy, lacking leadership

indicators.note: lacking leadership means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to feeling miserable and without direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, or own up, is to confess or acknowledge.

clue.text: Often the sound of the school was reduced

indicators.note: reduced means the word was is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: The noise of the school used to be quieter.
explanation.walkthrough: SCH, then WA: WAS with its last letter gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The schwa is the unstressed neutral vowel, the commonest vowel sound in English, as in 'the'.

clue.text: Song lyric? I could get you Leaving on a Jet Plane

definitions.text: I could get you Leaving on a Jet Plane

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
a line of a song is a lyric

explanation.surface: Quoting the song Leaving on a Jet Plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaving on a Jet Plane is a John Denver song; the definition reads it literally, as a trip by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier that flies passengers is the thing that gets you leaving on a jet plane.

clue.text: Top teacher keeping various tomes in residence

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are mixed up into a different order

explanation.surface: The headmaster keeps a variety of books at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A homestead is a house with its land, a dwelling.

clue.text: Remarkable article about male railway worker

indicators.note: about means the remarkable article goes around the male letter

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable or remarkable, as in a signal success
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A notable newspaper piece about a man who works on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable article' is read as one unit that goes around the male letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A signalman operates the signals and points on a railway line from a signal box.

clue.text: Injury besetting English team of women?

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the injury goes around English

parts.note: harm is injury or damage

explanation.surface: An injury crisis hits an English women's sports side.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a harem is a group of women, not a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a household in some traditions, a whimsical group or squad of females.

clue.text: First Lady's not without love? It happens

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: without means the love letter is dropped from the word not

parts.note: the letters of not, taken as written
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A president's wife is apparently not lacking in affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife, but it is Eve. Take O (love) out of NOT to get NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, an occurrence.

clue.text: Chance is at work, in pursuit of money for engineers

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the rearranged letters come after the money letter
at work suggests the letters are busily being reworked

explanation.surface: Luck plays its part when engineers chase cash.
explanation.walkthrough: M, followed by ECHANICS, the reworking of CHANCE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanics are skilled workers who repair and maintain machinery, a kind of engineer.

clue.text: Each recruit gets busy in 20's shop

definitions.note: 20 is BUTCHER, so this is a butcher's shop

indicators.note: gets busy suggests the letters bustle around into a new order

explanation.surface: Every new recruit is put to work at the meat counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 20 down is BUTCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A charcuterie is a delicatessen selling cooked and cured meats, a pork butcher's.

clue.text: Bit of grouse — a precise cut — fit for the stomach

indicators.note: bit of means just the opening letter of grouse is taken
cut means the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: strict means exact or precise

explanation.surface: A piece of game bird, carefully carved, suitable for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: G, then A, then STRIC: STRICT with its last letter cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the adjective meaning relating to the stomach.

clue.text: Favour light pop album

parts.note: grace means favour or goodwill
to light on, or alight, is to land

explanation.surface: A kind, gentle pop record.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceland is Paul Simon's 1986 album, a best-selling record.

clue.text: Devil's victim losing force before grave

indicators.note: losing means the force letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Faust sold his soul to the Devil (Mephistopheles) in the legend
F is the physics symbol for force
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A soul lost to the Devil, losing strength, heads towards the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective meaning stern. FAUST loses F to give AUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and grave both describe a severe, solemn, unsmiling manner.

clue.text: Farmworker has drink, tucking into a bit

indicators.note: tucking into means the drink goes inside

parts.note: a sherd is a fragment, a bit of broken pottery
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A labourer has a drink while eating a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it means going inside; a sherd is a broken fragment of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd is a person who tends pigs on a farm.

clue.text: Charlie, say, with excellent weapon

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass
eg, for example, is what say means
A1 means excellent; written AI

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie, for instance, with a first-rate weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' reads as a name, but in British slang a charlie is a fool, an ass. A1 (first-rate) is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Specific types of product for unexciting people

definitions.meaning: first meaning: products of a number multiplied by itself

explanation.walkthrough: In maths a product is the result of multiplying, and squares are a special kind of product.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means numbers multiplied by themselves and also old-fashioned, conformist people.

clue.text: Went up front of cliff displaying arms and legs

indicators.note: front of means just the opening letter of cliff

parts.note: limbed means having limbs, arms and legs

explanation.surface: A climber scaled the cliff face using every limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbed means ascended, as up a slope or ladder.

clue.text: Ruin arrangement of Schubert, omitting soprano

indicators.note: an arrangement of music rearranges, so the letters are reordered
omitting means the soprano letter is left out

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A poor arrangement of a Schubert work, without the soprano, spoils it.
explanation.walkthrough: SCHUBERT without S leaves CHUBERT, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher something is to botch or ruin it through clumsiness.

clue.text: Male comedians possibly brought in alien gear

indicators.note: brought in means the comedians go inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial
quip men: men who make quips, which male comedians might be called

explanation.surface: Male comics bring along some extraterrestrial kit.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIP MEN, a jokey name for male comedians, goes inside ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is the gear or apparatus needed for a task.

clue.text: Historic area producing foodstuff

parts.note: past means bygone, historic

explanation.surface: A historic region famous for its food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple food made from flour and water dough.

clue.text: Give good review to former group making comeback

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: making comeback means the group word is read from the end back

parts.note: a lot is a group or set

explanation.surface: A critic praises a band that has reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, then TOL: LOT read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, as a favourable review does.

clue.text: Cautious sort of line taken about old royal insignia

indicators.note: taken about means the line goes around the royal letters

parts.note: a ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A wary kind of line is followed around old royal symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: A ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient landmarks; ER (Elizabeth Regina) appeared on British postboxes and coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means wary or suspicious.

clue.text: Tapestry showing rows of figures, say, but excluding year

indicators.note: excluding means the year letter is left out

parts.note: arrays are arrangements of numbers in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A wall hanging depicts lines of people, apart from the year it was made.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich tapestry wall hanging, named after the French town.

clue.text: Sprays water on garden, adopting gardener's ultimate talisman?

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the last letter goes inside

parts.note: hoses means sprays with a hose

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of gardener's

parts.note: the gardener, with the possessive dropped
to hoe is to work the garden with a hoe

explanation.surface: A gardener waters and tends the plot while keeping a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here, meaning to work the soil with a hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Very popular place to stay offering reduction of 40%

indicators.note: a reduction of 40% means two of the five letters are lopped off the end, keeping the front three

parts.note: a hotel is a place to stay

explanation.surface: A hotel offers a big discount on rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Two of HOTEL's five letters are 40%; drop the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot means much in demand or fashionable.

clue.text: Break up, being badly misled about soldier

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the soldier
badly means the letters of misled are messed up

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ANT

explanation.surface: A misinformed squaddie is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: A soldier ant is a type of ant, so 'soldier' gives the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart into pieces.

clue.text: Obscene song showing change of heart

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letter of the song is swapped for another

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A rude song in which someone changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' sounds emotional, but it means the middle letter of DITTY becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty, of jokes or songs, means indecent or smutty.
